observations: All three photos show the same object wrapped tightly in clear plastic film, apparently a photocopier shape (box with flat top, control area outline).
Brand 'SHARP' and model 'AR-M207' are printed on the front panel, visible in photo 0 and photo 1.
A small 'digital' logo badge is visible in photo 1 on the side panel.
No control panel, display screen, paper trays, or power cable are clearly visible due to plastic wrap obscuring most detail.
No toner level, page counter, or power-on indicator is visible in any photo.
Seller watermark 'SMATECH MEGA EQUIPMENT' overlays all images; no additional context photos (e.g., open panel, test print, power-on screen) provided.

risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for parts

risks.risk: Drum, toner, or fuser unit condition unknown, could need costly replacement
risks.proof: Photo of open drum/toner compartment showing consumable levels and part condition
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming consumables need full replacement

risks.risk: Page/copy counter unknown, affecting remaining machine lifespan
risks.proof: Photo of the counter/display showing total page count

risks.risk: Physical damage hidden under plastic wrap (dents, cracked panels, missing parts)
risks.proof: Photos with plastic wrap fully removed from all sides
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic condition unknown, assume moderate wear

risks.risk: No visible power cord or accessories included
risks.proof: Photo showing power cable, drum unit, and any accessories included in sale
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare unit only, no accessories

proof_requests: Remove plastic wrap and photograph the full front with control panel visible
Power on the unit and show a photo/video of the display screen lit up
Produce a test copy/print and photograph the output along with the page counter reading
Open the toner/drum compartment and photograph consumable condition
Show the power cable and any included accessories
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a Sharp AR-M207 copier from visible branding, but no functional proof (power-on, test print, counter) is shown, so it must be priced at worst case as non-working/high-risk until such proof is provided.
